articles.title: Medicare Program; CY 2027 Inpatient Hospital Deductible and Hospital and Extended Care Services Coinsurance Amounts
articles.summary: This notice announces the inpatient hospital deductible and the hospital and extended care services coinsurance amounts for services furnished in calendar year (CY) 2027 under Medicare's Hospital Insurance Program (Medicare Part A). The Medicare statute specifies the formulae used to determine these amounts. For CY 2027, the inpatient hospital deductible will be $1,776. The daily coinsurance amounts for CY 2027 will be as follows: $444 for the 61st through 90th day of hospitalization in a benefit period; $888 for lifetime reserve days; and $222 for the 21st through 100th day of extended care services in a skilled nursing facility in a benefit period.

articles.title: Medicare Program; Medicare Part B Monthly Actuarial Rates, Premium Rates, and Annual Deductible Beginning January 1, 2027
articles.summary: This notice announces the monthly actuarial rates for aged (age 65 and over) and disabled (under age 65) beneficiaries enrolled in Part B of the Medicare Supplementary Medical Insurance (SMI) program beginning January 1, 2027. In addition, this notice announces the monthly premium for aged and disabled beneficiaries, the deductible for 2027, and the income-related monthly adjustment amounts to be paid by beneficiaries with modified adjusted gross income above certain threshold amounts. The monthly actuarial rates for 2027 are $418.70 for aged enrollees and $452.40 for disabled enrollees. The standard monthly Part B premium rate for all enrollees for 2027 is $209.40, which is equal to 50 percent of the monthly actuarial rate for aged enrollees (or approximately 25 percent of the expected average total cost of Part B coverage for aged enrollees). The 2027 premium is 3.2 percent or $6.50 higher than the 2026 standard premium rate of $202.90. The Part B deductible for 2027 is $292.00 for all Part B beneficiaries. If a beneficiary has to pay an income-related monthly adjustment amount, that individual will have to pay a total monthly premium of about 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost of Part B coverage. Beginning in 2023, certain Medicare enrollees who are 36 months post kidney transplant, and therefore no longer eligible for full Medicare coverage, can elect to continue Part B coverage of immunosuppressive drugs by paying a premium. articles.title: Restoring Flexibility To Support Head Start Program Access
articles.summary: In this final rule, the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) removes requirements from the Head Start Program Performance Standards (Performance Standards) to restore local flexibility to Head Start programs and improve access to quality services. Specifically, this final rule removes requirements related to wages and benefits that the Administration believes are not in line with the plain language of the Head Start Act and are costly and overly prescriptive for Head Start programs and staff. ACF estimates these changes will result in over $2 billion in future cost savings for Head Start programs. The rescissions in this final rule impact the costliest parts of the final rule published by the Office of Head Start (OHS) in 2024, Supporting the Head Start Workforce and Consistent Quality Programming.
